newsitem.title: USA: Hillenbrand sees some European losses in '97.
newsitem.headline: Hillenbrand sees some European losses in '97.

text.p: Hillenbrand Industries Inc said Tuesday that losses in certain European countries will continue to impact results in 1997.

"However, restructuring efforts, already well underway, are expected to reduce those losses," Gus Hillenbrand, president, said in a statement. "Overall, we are optimistic about the company's prospects for 1997."

Earlier, Hillenbrand reported earnings for the fourth quarter ended November 30 of $0.56 a share, up from year-ago results of $0.12 a share, which included a $0.37 a share charge. For fiscal 1996, it earned $2.02 a share, up from $1.27 a year ago. Excluding gains in 1996 and charges in 1995, fiscal 1996 earnings were $1.90 a share, up 16 percent.
Results for fiscal 1996 were hurt by lower European sales, which carry lower margins, the disposition of BLock Medical in July and lower sales at its Medeco Security Locks unit.
Hillenbrand said its fourth-quarter funeral segment revenues and operating profit grew compared with 1995.

Within funeral services, insurance revenues and operating profit at The ForeThought Group were up by double-digit rates. At Batesville Casket Co, revenues and operating profit were essentially flat, it added.
In the health care segment, fourth quarter revenues declined marginally but operating profit grew due to higher domestic volume, cost controls and a shift in the sales mix to higher margin products.
Strong domestic capital sales at Hill-Rom, which is part of the health care segment, were offset by reduced leels of lower margin European health care sales.

"New product introductions during 1996 and those anticipated in 1997 are expected to drive revenue growth in all of our businesses," Hillenbrand said. "Continuous improvement efforts throughout the company will continue to increase our productivity and quality."
